parsed.justification: Rationale A correctly identifies the comment as an explicit action (compare with linear regression) that is vague on execution details, mapping to a score of 3 on the rubric. Rationale B overstates the concreteness: while the method to compare against is named, the comment does not provide concrete details on how to implement the comparison (e.g., dataset, metrics, experimental setup), so B incorrectly justifies a score of 5. B's claim that the comment 'fully actionable with explicit and concrete details' is not well supported by the text.
